title: Unified Inference: PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes - 2026-03-04
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the product requirements (PRD), high-level design, roadmap themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and the initial release notes for the Unified Inference initiative. It is intended for product managers, engineering leads, solutions architects, and GTM stakeholders.

Summary: Unified Inference is a single developer-facing product that provides consistent API primitives, routing, observability, and economics controls across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. This doc describes the scope for the next major release (v1.0), acceptance criteria, key design decisions, rollout plan, and pricing recommendations.

Goals and success metrics

- Business goals:
  - Increase self-serve adoption by reducing onboarding time for model-based features (target: 30% reduction in time-to-first-successful-call).
  - Increase revenue from Dedicated and Private products by enabling easy upgrade path from Hosted (target: +25% net-new MRR in FY26 Q3–Q4).
  - Reduce 95th percentile request tail latency by 15% for typical chat workloads.

- Product success metrics:
  - Time-to-first-successful-call (median) <= 15 minutes for a new team using quickstart.
  - Model routing correctness >= 99.9% for supported fallbacks.
  - Unit cost reduction via batching/caching guidance: >= 12% improvement for target workloads within 30 days.
  - NPS for developer experience >= 40 in product surveys.

Scope (what's in v1.0)

- Unified API surface: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, and structured output with consistent parameters and response shapes across deployment modes.
- Smart routing: latency-first and cost-first routing policies with automated fallback to compatible quantized variants.
- Observability: per-route latency/cost breakdown, token-level accounting, and model-level quality signals.
- Controls & Optimize: UI and API hooks for batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles.
- Rollouts: canary and automatic fallback policy integration with traffic-splitting.
- Documentation and quickstarts for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Out of scope (v1.0)

- Per-tenant pluggable model registries for Private (defer to v1.1).
- Full multi-cloud private control-plane orchestration (partial on-prem support only).

Requirements (functional and non-functional)

Functional requirements:
1. Unified REST/SDK: single endpoint and SDK switch to control deployment target. Example: POST /v1/unified/generate with parameter "deployment_target": {hosted|dedicated|private}.
2. Routing policies: support at least two policy types (latency_first, cost_first) configurable per-route.
3. Model catalog API: list compatible model variants and their recommended quantization profiles.
4. Fallbacks: automatic fallback to predetermined model variants when primary model fails or capacity constrained. Fallbacks must preserve semantic compatibility (same tokenizer family or adapter mapping).
5. Observability API: per-request trace ID, token-level cost estimate, model selection metadata, and quality signal buckets (e.g., hallucination_score, refusal_rate).
6. Rollouts: support percentage-based traffic splits and canary window configuration via the Console and API.

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile <= 300ms for short chat-turns (<=256 tokens) in Hosted within US regions.
- Reliability: 99.9% API availability for Hosted tier; Dedicated SLAs per contract.
- Cost guidance: system must provide automated batching and caching recommendations with estimated cost savings.
- Security & compliance: support per-tenant KMS integration for Private; audit logs preserved for 365 days by default.

Acceptance criteria

- E2E tests for all API flows across Hosted/Dedicated/Private passing in CI.
- Performance benchmark: unified API meets latency SLOs on pre-defined workloads (chat/long-form/embedding).
- Documentation: Quickstart guides for each deployment mode with example CLI/SDK snippets and a migration checklist.
- Security review completed and compliance checklist signed off by Security team.

High-level design and architecture decisions

Design principles:
- One API, multiple runtimes: keep the public contract stable; implement routing and model variant selection in the control plane.
- Configuration-as-code: rollout policies and routing configs are versioned and deployable through the Console and API.
- Observability-first: include cost and quality signals as first-class telemetry to enable product-level decisions.

Components (overview):
- Unified API Gateway: single entrypoint for SDK and REST. Responsible for auth, request validation, and routing decisions.
- Control Plane: policy engine managing routing, rollout configuration, model catalog, and fallback rules.
- Serving Runtime(s): per-deployment-mode optimized runtimes (hosted runtime pool, dedicated GPU pools, and private on-prem adapters).
- Monitoring & Telemetry: centralized traces, token accounting, and model quality evaluator.

APIs & data contracts (examples)

- Request (simplified):

  POST /v1/unified/generate
  {
    "deployment_target": "hosted",
    "model": "redwood-7b-mk2",
    "policy": "latency_first",
    "input": "Write a short summary of the API design",
    "stream": false
  }

- Response (simplified):

  {
    "request_id": "rid-1234",
    "model": "redwood-7b-mk2.quant8",
    "tokens": [ ... ],
    "cost_estimate": "0.0012",
    "quality_signals": {"hallucination_score": "low"}
  }

Model catalog entry table (example)

| field | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| model_id | logical model id exposed to customers | redwood-7b-mk2 |
| variant | runtime-compatible variant | redwood-7b-mk2.fp16, redwood-7b-mk2.quant8 |
| recommended_policy | policy suggestion for workload | latency_first |
| expected_throughput | tokens/sec on p4d | 12k |

Security considerations

- All API calls must be TLS1.2+.
- Private customers must configure KMS keys; all model artifacts are encrypted at rest.
- Audit logs for model access and routing changes retained 365 days.

Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters)

- Q2 2026 (current): v1.0 launch focusing on Unified API, routing policies, basic rollout controls, and Console integration.
- Q3 2026: Dedicated onboarding flows, advanced quantization recommendations, and cost-optimization automation.
- Q4 2026: Private control plane enhancements, per-tenant model registries, multi-cloud Private orchestration pilot.
- Q1 2027: Advanced QoE features – A/B evaluation tied to prompt sets, automated model rollback on quality regressions.

Roadmap milestones (dates tentative)

1. 2026-03-15: Feature complete API + CI smoke tests.
2. 2026-04-05: Internal dogfood across three product teams.
3. 2026-04-20: Security & compliance sign-off.
4. 2026-05-05: Public beta for Hosted with opt-in Dedicated early access.
5. 2026-06-15: GA for Hosted, Dedicated early access expanded.

Pricing & packaging notes

Pricing principles:
- Keep simple developer-first entry price for Hosted to drive PLG adoption.
- Surface cost-optimization features as monetizable add-ons for Dedicated/Private (advanced Optimize recommendations, extended retention on cost telemetry).
- Offer migration credits for customers moving from Hosted to Dedicated.

Suggested pricing tiers (high-level)

- Hosted (Self-Serve): pay-as-you-go, per-token pricing variable by model family. Example: base rate 0.0006 / input token, 0.0012 / output token for base models; premium models +50%. Includes basic observability and 30-day telemetry retention.
- Dedicated (Committed): monthly reservation starting at $10k/month for 1 GPU-equivalent capacity with discounted per-token pricing and SLA. Add-ons: advanced Optimize (+$2k/mo), extended telemetry (+$1k/mo).
- Private (Enterprise): platform license + deployment fee; pricing tailored per-customer. Includes KMS, audit retention, and 24/7 enterprise support.

Packaging guidance:
- Bundle migration playbook and one migration-assist month for any Dedicated contract > $50k ARR.
- For Private pilots, include a 3-month professional services block to handle on-prem packaging and network integration.

Release notes (v1.0 - March 2026 beta -> GA plan)

Highlights in beta (internal dogfood):
- Unified API endpoint implemented with parity across SDKs (Python, JS, Go).
- Routing policies (latency_first, cost_first) with simple policy DSL in Console.
- Per-request token accounting and basic cost estimates returned in responses.

Known limitations for beta:
- Private deployment installer only supports Ubuntu 22.04 and a subset of network topologies.
- Some older quantized model variants need kernel tuning for P4d; they will be optimized in Q3.

GA checklist:
- Performance & load testing scaled to 2x expected initial production traffic.
- SDK docs, migration guides, and quickstarts published.
- Customer success templates for Dedicated onboarding prepared.

Rollout plan & operational runbook summary

1. Internal dogfood (2026-04-05): product, platform, and ops teams. Monitor 95th percentile latency and error rates.
2. Private alpha (selected partners): validate Private installer and KMS integration.
3. Hosted public beta (opt-in) 2 weeks after private alpha success.
4. Expand to Dedicated early access customers with migration assistance.
5. GA: enable self-serve for Hosted and sales-assisted upgrade paths for Dedicated/Private.

Appendices

A. Quickstart snippets (Python):

from redwood import UnifiedClient
client = UnifiedClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-7b-mk2", input="Summarize the release notes", deployment_target="hosted")
print(resp.text)

B. Migration checklist (Hosted -> Dedicated):
1. Inventory active routes and models.
2. Run the cost estimator for three representative workloads.
3. Provision Dedicated capacity (initially 1 GPU-equivalent).
4. Run smoke tests and verify telemetry.
5. Schedule cutover with customer and enable canary traffic split.
